source_snapshot.purpose_facts: The title indicates a correctable processor-error test under an NV CPU RAS set, but the source supplies no executable or acceptance semantics beyond that label.
procedure_facts: Before-test text asks for recipe conformity and log clearing.
After-test text asks for result/photo collection and unexpected-log review.
criteria_facts: The entire acceptance criteria field is `TBD`.
missing_source_information: Exact NVIDIA CPU/platform generation and supported OS/firmware matrix.
Authoritative injector, exact command, correctable error type and processor target semantics.
Required target coverage and iteration count.
Expected native event, severity, freshness, timeout and no-reset/health behavior.
Safety authorization, recovery, restoration and pass/fail rules.

original_test_intent.statement: The recoverable source intent is only to validate a correctable processor RAS event on an unspecified NVIDIA CPU platform; its target, stimulus, coverage and acceptance behavior are not defined well enough to authorize execution.
must_preserve: Processor rather than memory, GPU, PCIe or platform error class.
Correctable rather than uncorrectable or fatal severity.
NVIDIA CPU platform scope, after the owner identifies the exact architecture.
must_not_infer: That `NV CPU` necessarily means Grace, BlueField or any particular product.
That generic Linux APEI EINJ is the intended or supported injector.
A core, socket, MPIDR/APIC-equivalent target, error subtype, iteration count or expected record.
That absence of a reset, presence of one log line or a tool return code constitutes PASS.

v2_review_conclusion.summary: V2 correctly identifies a genuine semantic blocker: both Procedure and Criteria are TBD, so no safe command, target or acceptance gate exists. It allows read-only baseline collection and prohibits inventing an injector.
v2_review_conclusion.specific_gap: No material classification error was found. V3 makes explicit that public Grace/EINJ capability evidence cannot identify this row's platform or replace an owner-authored recipe, and separates currently safe inventory from completion of the blocked test.

related_records: Neighboring Intel, AMD, BlueField, Grace, memory and GPU RAS cases cannot provide this row's missing NVIDIA CPU processor-correctable procedure by analogy.
applicable_history.precedence_application: The source title constrains only broad intent; its literal TBD Procedure and Criteria take precedence over generic public mechanisms or neighboring recipes.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Maintain V2 BLOCKED because the test's stimulus, target scope and acceptance semantics are absent, not merely because a package is unavailable. Permit only non-mutating platform and RAS-capability discovery until an authoritative owner replaces both TBD fields and the case is re-reviewed.

conditions_present: A processor-correctable RAS objective, NV CPU test-set label, generic pre/post collection steps and 10/10-minute estimates are present.
missing: Exact platform, authoritative procedure, injector/package, target and coverage, correctable signature, timeout, no-reset/health criteria, approval, recovery and restoration.
provider: NVIDIA/ODM FAE identifies the exact CPU platform and supplies the supported RAS injection specification/tool.
Test owner defines required processor target coverage, expected evidence and pass/fail criteria.
Platform/lab owner supplies a dedicated SUT, console/recovery path and action approvals.
safe_read_only_work: Inventory the CPU/platform, firmware, OS/kernel, ACPI tables, kernel RAS configuration and currently exposed injection capabilities without writing to them.
Export timestamped native OS, BMC and firmware RAS baselines without clearing logs.
Compare discovered capabilities with the eventual signed recipe; discovery alone cannot select or execute an injector.
prohibited_until_resolved: Log clear, BIOS/debug changes, module/configuration changes, writes to any injection interface, vendor-tool execution, fault stimulus, reset, retry or PASS/FAIL claim.
closure_evidence: Owner-authored Procedure and Criteria replace both TBD fields and name the exact supported platform/tool/version.
Signed target/coverage, command, expected correctable event, timeout, health, recovery and restoration rules pass a fresh case-specific review.
Dedicated-SUT and per-action approvals are recorded before execution.

revision_candidate.test_name: NVIDIA CPU Processor Correctable Error Injection - Definition Required
revision_candidate.purpose: After an authoritative platform-specific recipe is supplied, validate that one or more explicitly defined NVIDIA CPU processor targets report the specified correctable RAS event without an unapproved reset or loss of platform health. The current row does not yet define an executable test.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Unresolved. The owner must identify whether this is Grace, BlueField or another NVIDIA CPU architecture and provide the exact module/system, stepping, firmware, BIOS/BMC, OS/kernel and supported RAS injection mechanism. Do not transfer a recipe between these platforms.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Unresolved processor target and coverage. The eventual recipe must define core/socket/die or architecture-specific identifiers, processor error subtype, required iterations and whether every eligible target or a signed subset is in scope. The 10/10-minute values are estimates, not a test duration or timeout.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Exact platform identity; authoritative NVIDIA/ODM RAS specification; injector/tool/interface and version/hash; package and privilege requirements; supported firmware/OS/kernel; target/error-type map and coverage; exact command/trigger; expected native event identity, corrected severity, counter delta, timeout and no-reset/health behavior; baseline/clear policy; dedicated SUT; approvals; evidence retention; recovery and restoration.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: No injection command is authorized while Procedure and Criteria remain TBD. Perform only non-mutating inventory and capability discovery. After the owner replaces both TBD fields, submit the completed platform-specific procedure for a fresh V3 review; only that reviewed version may define baseline handling, one bounded approved injection, evidence correlation, recovery and restoration.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Both TBD fields replaced by an authoritative signed recipe; exact platform/tool/target/coverage/evidence resolved; dedicated non-production SUT; stable baseline; console/OOB, boot media, storage and recovery proven; all configuration, injection, reset, retry and restoration actions individually authorized.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Before execution can be authorized: signed platform identity, tool/spec, target/coverage, command, expected event fields, timeout, safety and recovery contract. For a future reviewed execution: exact identities/hashes, baseline audit, target mapping, command/transcript, fresh native-OS processor-correctable record correlated to the target within timeout, prescribed counter change, proof of no unexpected reset/degradation, health/recovery/restoration evidence and engineer disposition. Current read-only inventory is evidence of readiness only, not test completion.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: Not yet defined. The owner must provide the exact NVIDIA/ODM platform RAS specification and testcase-specific criteria. Public documentation showing that a platform or Linux can expose a processor-correctable injection type establishes possible capability only and is not this case's acceptance rule.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Do not choose an injector from the title, assume generic EINJ support, infer target identifiers, copy another NVIDIA/Arm/x86 recipe, clear logs, change BIOS/debug state, load or configure an injection path, write an error type/target/trigger, inject, reset, auto-retry or claim PASS/FAIL until the reviewed recipe exists. Never test production or management-critical workloads and never expose credentials or private artifacts.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: NVIDIA/ODM FAE and test owner must author and approve the missing procedure, criteria, platform/tool/target semantics and expected result. Platform/lab owner approves the dedicated SUT and recovery. A fresh reviewer approves the executable contract; a qualified operator authorizes and supervises every later state change and injection.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Before re-review, an Agent may only collect non-mutating inventory and baselines. Humans own recipe creation, target selection, configuration, injection authorization and recovery. After a future approved contract, Agent and operator boundaries must be defined by that contract; engineering retains PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED judgment.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: No recovery action is authorized by the current row because no stimulus is authorized. Preserve any accidental-change evidence, stop and escalate to the platform owner. The replacement recipe must define normal and failed-injection recovery, restoration and final health before execution.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Procedure or Criteria remains TBD; platform/tool/target/coverage/error semantics or expected record is unresolved; only analogous or generic documentation is available; approval, dedicated SUT, baseline, timeout, console, recovery, evidence storage or restoration is missing; discovered capabilities do not match the signed replacement recipe; or any unreviewed state change or injection is proposed.

identified_defects: The during-test Procedure is entirely TBD.
The NV CPU label does not identify a product architecture or supported injection path.
No target, coverage, command, expected event, timeout, health behavior or recovery exists.
reason_for_change: No V2 conclusion change is justified: this is a genuine semantic blocker, and public evidence of possible Grace or Linux injection support cannot safely author the missing testcase.

new_technical_evidence.title: Platform Software Patches and Configurations: Grace
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Only if the owner confirms the tested NV CPU platform is NVIDIA Grace
new_technical_evidence.supports: Grace partner diagnostics can require `CONFIG_ACPI_APEI_EINJ=m`, showing a possible standard injection mechanism on a specifically configured Grace Linux platform.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The source row does not say it is Grace, identify firmware support, or specify EINJ as the intended injector.

new_technical_evidence.title: APEI Error INJection
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Linux systems whose firmware exposes the relevant ACPI EINJ capability
new_technical_evidence.supports: The interface advertises supported types and defines `0x1` as Processor Correctable, while target parameters and vendor extensions depend on firmware/vendor documentation.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Capability, target semantics, trigger behavior and acceptance for this unspecified NVIDIA platform are unknown; this source does not authorize a command.

new_technical_evidence.title: Source testcase Wistron-System RAS-00820-V002
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Only this NV CPU processor-correctable row
new_technical_evidence.supports: The test name, test set, generic before/after text, literal TBD Procedure and literal TBD Criteria.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: All executable and acceptance semantics are absent.

removed_ambiguities: States that NV CPU is not enough to identify Grace, BlueField or another architecture.
Distinguishes read-only capability discovery from execution or completion.
Prevents generic EINJ capability from being substituted for the missing owner recipe.
remaining_blockers: The exact platform, procedure, criteria, tool, target/coverage, expected evidence, timeout, safety and recovery contract are all unresolved; the test remains BLOCKED until the source is rewritten and re-reviewed.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V2 was already technically correct, so KEEP is the evidence-based outcome; V3 adds explicit product-identity and public-capability boundaries without pretending that clarification resolves either TBD field.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The contract-only validator correctly refused to select Grace, BlueField, EINJ, a target or an injection command; distinguished readiness inventory from test completion; and identified the source document and platform handoff as the blockers. It made no executable plan and found BLOCKED justified until a signed replacement is freshly reviewed.
